hook.line: Tomás wants the café's reopening to be a night people talk about. Spanish has two short phrases for doing something big, with no expense spared.
hook.es: Si vamos a abrir el café, lo hacemos a lo grande.
hook.en: If we're going to open the café, we're doing it big.

examples.es: Celebraron el grado por todo lo alto.
examples.en: They celebrated the graduation in style.

examples.es: Mariana vive a lo grande aunque gana poco.
examples.en: Mariana lives it up even though she earns little.

examples.es: Quiero celebrar mi cumpleaños a lo grande.
examples.en: I want to celebrate my birthday in a big way.

examples.es: Rosa celebraba la Navidad a lo grande.
examples.en: Rosa used to celebrate Christmas in a big way.

examples.es: Si vamos a abrir el café, lo hacemos a lo grande.
examples.en: If we're going to open the café, we're doing it big.
Are we going to celebrate in a big way?

examples.es: Lo celebramos por todo lo alto.

rule:
*A lo grande* and *por todo lo alto* both mean "in a big way, in style, no expense spared". They go after the verb: *celebrar*, *vivir*, *hacer*, *viajar*.
They describe how you do it, so they work like English "in style" or "go big".
The little words are fixed: *a lo grande*, never *en lo grande*, and *por todo lo alto* keeps its *lo*. Beware *alto*: here it has nothing to do with loud.
*Por todo lo alto* is a touch more elegant. Related: *echar la casa por la ventana*, to splurge.
smallPrint: Teachers call these adverbial phrases: fixed groups that describe how something is done.

readAndPick.es: Celebraron el grado por todo lo alto.
options: They celebrated the graduation in style.

readAndPick.es: Hicieron la boda a lo grande.
Mariana vive a lo grande aunque gana poco.
options: Mariana lives simply because she earns little.
Mariana lives it up even though she earns little.

readAndPick.es: Si vamos a abrir el café, lo hacemos a lo grande.
options: If we open the café, we'll do it big.
If we open the café, we'll do it small.

readAndPick.es: Rosa celebraba la Navidad a lo grande.
options: Rosa is going to celebrate Christmas in a big way.
Rosa used to celebrate Christmas in a big way.

readAndPick.es: Lo celebramos por todo lo alto.
options: We said it in a loud voice.

readAndPick.es: No vivo a lo grande, pero vivo bien.
options: I don't live extravagantly, but I live well.
I live extravagantly, but I don't live well.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *a lo grande* or *en lo grande*, then type the whole sentence: Vive ___. (He lives the high life.)
yourTurn.why: The fixed phrase is *a lo grande*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *por todo lo alto* or *por todo alto*, then type the whole sentence: Celebraron el grado ___. (They celebrated the graduation in style.)
yourTurn.answer: Celebraron el grado por todo lo alto.
yourTurn.why: The *lo* stays in *por todo lo alto*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I want to celebrate my birthday in a big way.
yourTurn.answer: Quiero celebrar mi cumpleaños a lo grande.
accept: Quiero celebrar mi cumpleaños por todo lo alto.
yourTurn.why: The phrase goes after what you are celebrating.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: If we're going to open the café, we're doing it big.
yourTurn.answer: Si vamos a abrir el café, lo hacemos a lo grande.
accept: Si vamos a abrir el café, lo hacemos por todo lo alto.
yourTurn.why: *Lo hacemos* is "we do it", and the phrase says how.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Rosa used to celebrate Christmas in a big way.
yourTurn.answer: Rosa celebraba la Navidad a lo grande.
accept: Rosa celebraba la Navidad por todo lo alto.
Rosa celebraba Navidad a lo grande.
yourTurn.why: *Celebraba* is the habit in the past.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Vivo a lo grande.* becomes: I don't live extravagantly.
Make it a question: *Vamos a celebrar a lo grande.* becomes: Are we going to celebrate in a big way?
accept: ¿Vamos a celebrar por todo lo alto?
yourTurn.why: Spanish adds the question marks; the words stay the same.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The fixed phrase uses *a*, not *en*.

pitfalls.wrong: Celebraron el grado por todo alto.
pitfalls.right: Celebraron el grado por todo lo alto.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Lo* is part of the fixed phrase.
Almost. Spanish doesn't turn *grande* into an adverb here, it uses the fixed phrase.

personal: Tell me one thing you would do *a lo grande* if you could.
